title: Sprint-anchored release-train handover template and comms playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As we scale concurrent launches across runtime, console, and API surfaces, the handoff moments between sprint teams and the release-train lead are a repeated source of misalignment: unclear cutover owners, mismatched rollout windows, and ad-hoc comms that create last-minute throttles and regional capacity spikes.

Goal: Create a lightweight, sprint-anchored handover template plus a comms playbook that standardizes signals, owners, and contingency lanes for every release-train cohort. The deliverable should be a one-page template for engineering teams and a short playbook for PMs/ops with runbook links and escalation trees.

Scope: Runtime, Console, API changes that are gated by the quarterly release-train calendar. Excludes emergency hotfix paths and platform infra-only upgrades (those follow the infra runbook).

Success metrics (1 month post-adoption):
- Reduction in last-minute rollout scope changes > 50%
- < 1 production rollback attributable to handoff miscommunication per quarter
- 90% of launches include completed template before code freeze

Proposed deliverables:
1) Handover template (single page): required pre-cutover checklist, owners, traffic lanes, blackout windows, capacity signals (expected qps/token-rate), verified rollout knobs, and fall-forward/fallback model mappings.
2) Comms playbook (two pages): stakeholder roster, templated stakeholder announcements, escalation matrix (on-call, release-train lead, paging), and post-launch survey questions for ops.
3) Integration examples: show one filled template for a runtime quantization rollout and one for a Console UI toggle release.
4) Automation hooks: spec for a calendar-as-code snippet that populates release-train calendar entries from the template (hand off to ENG infra).

Out-of-scope for this ticket: building the calendar automation; this ticket produces the spec and examples only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Template created and reviewed by at least 2 runtime leads, 1 console PM, and 1 API owner.
- Playbook reviewed and signed off by Release Train Lead and Head of SRE.
- Two example templates completed (runtime quantization, console feature flag).
- Playbook PR merged to doc site and linked from release calendar.
- Quickstart 10-minute enablement doc + 30-minute async training recorded and uploaded.

risks:
- If ENG infra does not deliver calendar-as-code spec on schedule, teams may not adopt the automation; mitigation: include manual calendar copy-paste instructions.
- Cross-team reviewers may request extensive changes; mitigation: lock mandatory fields and mark optional ones to keep the template concise.
- Regional capacity numbers might be stale; mitigation: require SRE signoff on capacity signals before template acceptance.
stakeholders: Runtime Engineering Leads - Jordan Kim, Nia Okoye
open_questions:
- Should rollback criteria include automated traffic shifting, or is manual operator intervention required per team?
- What minimal telemetry must be present to mark a rollout 'green' inside the template?
- How do we represent mixed-surface launches (e.g., runtime model upgrade + console UX change) in a single template?
